summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (top hypothesis H1, 0.78; Critic-accepted): infra-automation applied cfg-2207 at 09:52:00Z, cutting portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 under a 'cost-optimisation profile small'. The pool, which had a steady-state working set of ~12 connections, immediately shrank to and pinned at exactly 5.0 (HikariPool total=5/active=5/idle=0, waiting=43), producing 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' errors from 09:53:19Z and driving portfolio-service p99 above the gateway's upstream timeout, so api-gateway returned 504 upstream-timeout on /v1/portfolio/* from 09:53:53Z. The gateway deploy dep-5220 (08:00Z, envoy/HTTP-2) is coincidental - the gateway is the reporter, not the origin: its CPU/memory stay flat and no GOAWAY/stream-reset fingerprints appear in its WARN logs. A shared-datastore origin (H3) is excluded by measurement: ledger-db co-tenants order-service and payment-service, plus redis-cache co-tenant auth-service, all stay flat through the onset window.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service datasource pool cut to 5 by cfg-2207 causes JDBC starvation → gateway 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: infra-automation applied cfg-2207 at 09:52:00Z reducing portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 under a 'cost-optimisation profile small'. portfolio-service's steady-state working set was ~12 connections, so a 5-connection pool is immediately oversubscribed: the pool stepped down 11.98 → 8.45 (09:52) → flatlined at exactly 5.0 from 09:54, HikariPool reported total=5/active=5/idle=0 with waiting=43, and GET /v1/portfolio/holdings began failing with 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' at 09:53:19Z. portfolio-service p99 rose to ~4.1-4.3s, exceeding the gateway's upstream timeout, so api-gateway returned 504 upstream-timeout on /v1/portfolio/* from 09:53:53Z. The gateway deploy dep-5220 (08:00Z) is coincidental; the gateway is the reporter, not the origin (its CPU/memory stay flat).

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 exists in the change feed: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52:00Z by infra-automation cost-optimisation profile
cfg-2207 was actually applied to the running portfolio-service instance at ~09:52:13Z (portfolio-service logs 'config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5')
portfolio-service's working set was ~12 connections (db_pool_in_use avg 11.98 pre-onset), so a 5-connection pool is immediately oversubscribed
Pool collapses on the config boundary: db_pool_in_use steps 11.98 -> 8.45 (09:52) -> flatlines at exactly 5.0 from 09:54 on; HikariPool total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43
Requests block on JDBC acquisition and fail: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' from 09:53:19Z, 66s after cfg-2207 applied
portfolio-service p99 jumps to 1865ms (09:50 bucket) then ~4100-4300ms, matching the pool collapse onset; its own CPU/memory are flat
portfolio-service latency exceeds the gateway's upstream timeout, producing upstream-timeout 504s: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' from 09:53:53Z, 252/255 WARNs
Gateway p99 hits 4.4s and 5xx ~7% while its own CPU/memory stay flat — gateway is the reporter, not the origin

No shared-datastore origin: ledger-db co-tenants order-service and payment-service stay completely healthy (flat p99 ~149ms/~320ms, flat ~0.2% error rate) across the onset window, isolating the anomaly to portfolio-service

assumptions: portfolio-service holds (roughly) one DB connection per in-flight request, so pool size bounds concurrency

redis-cache co-tenants (market-data-service, auth-service) were not fully checked; but redis is on portfolio-service's read path only and no cache error signature appears, so a redis origin is not supported

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway dep-5220 envoy/HTTP-2 upgrade caused upstream timeouts on high-fanout /v1/portfolio/* routes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5220 upgraded envoy 1.29->1.30 and enabled HTTP/2 to upstreams at 08:00Z. Newer HTTP/2 concurrency defaults or connection handling on the high-fanout portfolio route caused upstream request deadlines to be exceeded, so the gateway logged 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' 504s. This is the reporter's suspicion and matches the historic precedent HIST-116. It requires the deploy's effect to stay dormant for ~1h50m and then coincide exactly with a backend DB-pool config change.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 deployed 08:00Z: envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service
New HTTP/2 connection handling / max-concurrent-streams defaults cause head-of-line blocking or stream starvation on the high-fanout portfolio route
Requests to portfolio-service exceed the gateway's upstream timeout, producing 504 upstream timeouts
Gateway p99 rises to >4s and gateway 5xx to ~7%

assumptions: The 08:00 deploy's effect could lay dormant ~1h50m and only bite at 09:52 — no mechanism for this delay is evidenced
Historic HIST-116's rollback resolution transfers to today's envoy version

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db (or redis-cache) degradation behind portfolio-service causing portfolio 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: portfolio-service's direct dependency ledger-db (shared with order-service and payment-service) or redis-cache (shared with auth-service and market-data-service) degraded, slowing portfolio-service queries and exhausting its connection pool, surfacing as gateway 504s. Precedent HIST-102 shows portfolio timeouts during a ledger-db failover. This is now contradicted by verified co-tenant measurements: order-service and payment-service, both on ledger-db, stay completely flat through the onset window, and auth-service (redis co-tenant) is flat at ~90ms.

causal_chain.claim: Shared ledger-db/redis-cache are in portfolio-service's direct dependency path [and order/payment/auth paths]
ledger-db or redis-cache degrades, queries slow down and connections are held longer
portfolio-service pool exhausts: HikariPool active=5, waiting=43
portfolio-service p99 blows up and gateway returns upstream-timeout 504s
REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: ledger-db co-tenants order-service and payment-service show no latency or error-rate anomaly at 09:45-09:55Z or after, although both share ledger-db with portfolio-service
REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: redis-cache co-tenant auth-service p99 is flat ~90ms across the entire window

assumptions: A DB-side slowdown coincided with the 09:52 pool change — untested, and the sharp simultaneous onset at gateway+portfolio plus the pool pinning exactly at the new limit of 5.0 argues against an independent DB slowdown
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: A shared-datastore fault would degrade all co-tenants. Verified measurements show ledger-db co-tenants order-service (p99 flat 144.97-153.40ms, error ~0.2%) and payment-service (p99 flat ~320ms, error ~0.2%) completely healthy through 09:30-11:57, and redis-cache co-tenant auth-service flat ~90ms. The fault is isolated to portfolio-service alone, and the pool pinned at exactly the new limit of 5.0 immediately on the cfg-2207 boundary (09:52-09:54), which a DB-side slowdown would not produce.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Pure capacity saturation of portfolio-service DB connections with no faulty change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Portfolio request load outgrew the provisioned DB connection capacity with no triggering change, exhausting the pool and queueing requests until the gateway timed out.

causal_chain.claim: Request volume to /v1/portfolio/* rose past usable connection capacity
Pool saturates: db_pool_in_use pinned at 5.0, waiting=43
Gateway upstream timeouts -> 504s

assumptions: The change to 5 is coincidental rather than causal
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Pre-onset db_pool_in_use averaged ~11.98, far below the prior limit of 50; the pool pinned at exactly the new limit of 5.0 immediately on the cfg-2207 boundary. Capacity was deliberately reduced, not outgrown.

facts.statement: Exactly two config changes occurred on 2026-03-10: order-service cfg-2199 (log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2, 07:00Z) and portfolio-service cfg-2207 (db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52:00Z, by infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource').

portfolio-service logged cfg-2207 being applied to the live instance at 09:52:13Z ('config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5'), 13 seconds after the change timestamp and before any JDBC error.
portfolio-service's DB connection pool sat at ~11.5-12.9 connections until 09:50 (avg 11.98), dropped to 8.45 at 09:52, and flatlined at exactly 5.0 from 09:54 onwards.

The first 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' error is at 09:53:19Z, 66 seconds after cfg-2207 was applied; HikariPool-1 exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) is first logged at 09:54:29Z and recurs with waiting 25-57.

The earliest gateway 504 is an 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' at 09:53:53Z, 34 seconds AFTER the first portfolio-service JDBC acquire failure; this pattern accounts for 252 of 255 WARN entries.
portfolio-service p99 rose from ~180ms (through 09:45) to ~4.1-4.3s, exceeding the gateway upstream timeout; latency onset is sharp and simultaneous with the pool collapse.
api-gateway CPU (mean 42.01%, max 46.78%) and memory (mean 57.94%, max 64.22%) are flat and unsaturated across the entire window including the onset period.

Only one deployment exists in the window: dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00Z (envoy 1.29 -> 1.30, HTTP/2 to upstreams for portfolio-service and order-service), status live with no rollback recorded.
No GOAWAY / stream-reset / HTTP/2 fingerprints appear in the gateway's WARN patterns; the dominant pattern is upstream timeout to portfolio-service.

No DB-slowdown signature precedes the pool exhaustion: searches for 'slow', 'deadlock' and 'ledger' on portfolio-service over 09:00-10:30Z returned 0 matches; only JDBC-acquire and HikariPool timeout patterns are present.

ledger-db co-tenants order-service and payment-service stay healthy through the onset window: order-service p99 in a 144.97-153.40ms band and error_rate flat ~0.2%; payment-service p99 flat ~320ms and error_rate flat ~0.2%.
redis-cache co-tenant auth-service p99 stayed flat ~90ms (min 79.72, max 98.88) across the entire 08:00-11:59 window.
portfolio-service CPU is flat across the window (mean 36.0, max 39.78), so its latency blowup is not explained by its own CPU/memory pressure.

portfolio-service's direct dependencies are ledger-db, market-data-service and redis-cache; ledger-db and redis-cache are shared, so a fault there would also affect order-service/payment-service and auth-service/market-data-service.

assumptions: portfolio-service holds roughly one DB connection per in-flight request, so pool size bounds concurrency.
redis-cache co-tenants were not fully checked, but redis is on portfolio-service's read path only and no cache error signature appears, so a redis origin is not supported.
Inference (not assumption) that the pool collapse at the cfg-2207 boundary, rather than an independent DB slowdown, caused the starvation rests on the ordering evidence in F19/F20/F22/F23/F24.

timeline.event: Dep-5220 deployed: api-gateway v9.3.0, envoy 1.29 -> 1.30, HTTP/2 enabled to upstreams (portfolio-service, order-service). No rollback recorded.
Last normal bucket: gateway p99 ~200ms, error_rate ~0.2%; portfolio-service p99 ~180ms.
Onset: gateway p99 jumps to avg 1849.99ms / max 4418.76ms; portfolio-service p99 to 1865.15ms; db_pool_in_use still ~11.98 until 09:50.
cfg-2207 change timestamp: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 by infra-automation; db_pool_in_use drops to 8.45.
DB pool flatlines at exactly 5.0 and remains pinned through 10:10 and beyond.
First portfolio-service error: GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed - could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms.
First gateway 504: upstream timeout to portfolio-service on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings.
First HikariPool-1 exhaustion log: total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43; recurs with waiting 25-57.
Incident INC-002 reported by on-call SRE: portfolio page spinning/timing out, gateway p99 > 4s, 504s on /v1/portfolio/*.
Gateway upstream-timeout 504s to portfolio-service continue through the end of data (252 of 255 WARNs in this pattern).

recommended_actions.action: Immediately revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 5 to 50 (its pre-change value) rather than rolling back the gateway deploy dep-5220.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool pinned at exactly the new limit of 5.0 immediately on the cfg-2207 boundary (09:52-09:54) while pre-onset demand averaged 11.98, and JDBC acquire failures began 66s after the change and 34s before the first gateway 504. Reverting the pool setting removes the actual bottleneck; a gateway rollback addresses a non-causal change.

recommended_actions.action: Verify mitigation by confirming db_pool_in_use rises above 5 (no longer pinned), HikariPool waiting returns to 0, 'could not acquire JDBC connection' errors stop, and gateway p99/error_rate return to baseline (~200ms / ~0.2%).
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact signals that degraded: pool pinning at 5.0 with waiting=43, JDBC-acquire failures, and gateway 504 upstream timeouts to portfolio-service.

recommended_actions.action: Audit and gate the 'cost-optimisation profile small' application: add a pre-apply validation that rejects datasource pool sizes below observed steady-state working-set demand (e.g. require pool >= p95 of db_pool_in_use), and require manual approval for pool-size reductions.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 was applied automatically by infra-automation and reduced the pool to 5 against a ~12-connection working set; the same class of change (HIST-115: 'datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile') has recurred.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on DB pool saturation and gateway upstream-timeout rate (e.g. db_pool_in_use at max with waiting > 0; gateway 504 'upstream timeout <service>') with a threshold well below 3s.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool was pinned at exactly 5.0 with waiting=43 and gateway 504s ran 09:53:53Z to 11:58:44Z; earlier detection would have shortened the ~2h outage.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT treat dep-5220 (envoy/HTTP-2) as the origin; close it out as coincidental but retain the HTTP/2 stream-starvation check as a regression test, since no GOAWAY/stream-reset fingerprints were observed.
recommended_actions.rationale: Gateway CPU/memory are flat, its 504s are all upstream timeouts to portfolio-service, and the JS-attributable timing aligns with cfg-2207 rather than the 08:00Z deploy that preceded onset by 1h52m.

recommended_actions.action: Exercise the fallback hypothesis only if the pool revert does not restore service: then investigate a shared-datastore (ledger-db/redis-cache) origin, using ledger-db's connections_active/slow_queries_per_min/replication_lag_ms and redis-cache's hit_ratio_pct/evictions_per_min.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3 is currently contradicted by healthy ledger-db co-tenants (order-service, payment-service) and redis-cache co-tenant auth-service, but datastore-side series were never retrieved; this is the discriminating check if the primary fix fails.

recommended_actions.action: Post-incident review to institutionalise the precedent (HIST-115/HIST-116): add pool-size change reviews and gateway HTTP/2 upgrade verification to the standard change checklist.
recommended_actions.rationale: This incident matched a prior pool-override (HIST-115) while the reporter's suspicion matched a different precedent (HIST-116), so the checklist should distinguish the two signatures.

data_gaps: No metric data could be retrieved for api-gateway, portfolio-service, ledger-db or redis-cache via query_metrics within the turn budget, so onset timing had to be inferred from log lines rather than telemetry; exact onset second is from logs (09:53:19Z portfolio-service).
No rollback of dep-5220 and no config change reverting cfg-2207 is recorded as of 2026-03-10T11:59Z, so it is unknown whether any mitigation occurred or whether the incident was still ongoing.

portfolio-service WARN/ERROR logs for 09:00-11:59Z could not be retrieved (query_logs returned budget_exhausted), so the backend error signature for the pool exhaustion is unverified beyond the acquire-failure and HikariPool lines.

ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms or error_rate metrics (only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), and redis-cache exposes no latency/error metrics either; those datastore-side series could not be retrieved due to budget exhaustion, so H3 exclusion rests on co-tenant service metrics only.
market-data-service latency/error metrics and auth-service error_rate queries returned budget_exhausted and were never executed, leaving market-data-service (a redis-cache co-tenant) unchecked.

No dedicated HTTP/2 or upstream connection-pool/thread metrics exist for api-gateway, so HTTP/2-specific connection signatures are unverified beyond the absence of GOAWAY/stream-reset strings in WARN patterns.
api-gateway and portfolio-service metric buckets are 300s wide, so metric onset can only be bounded to the 09:50-09:55 window.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: If reverting cfg-2207 (pool back to 50) does NOT restore portfolio-service and gateway latency to baseline, H1 would be falsified.

If ledger-db's own series (connections_active, slow_queries_per_min, replication_lag_ms) showed a simultaneous anomaly at 09:45-09:55Z, or if additional ledger-db co-tenants degraded, H3 would become viable.
If gateway logs contained GOAWAY / stream-reset / HTTP/2 max-concurrent-stream errors aligning with the 08:00Z deploy, that would support H2 over H1.
If db_pool_in_use were shown to have exceeded the old limit of 50 (rather than pinning at the new limit of 5.0 on the config boundary), pure capacity saturation (H4) would re-open.
If the cfg-2207 'applied' log line at 09:52:13Z were shown to be a no-op (pool still at 50), the causal link between cfg-2207 and the pool pinning at 5.0 would break.

findings.statement: No DB-slowdown signature precedes the pool exhaustion: searches over 09:00–10:30Z for 'slow' and 'deadlock' on portfolio-service returned 0 matches, and 'ledger' returned 0 matches. The only patterns present are the JDBC-acquire failure (77 by 10:29) and HikariPool timeout (70), plus benign INFO lines. There is no slow-query, DB-timeout, deadlock or ledger-db error before or after the pool pins.

Interpretation: the ordering — config-applied → pool shrinks to 5 → acquire failures with a saturated 5-connection pool → gateway 504s, with zero preceding DB-latency/timeout/deadlock evidence — matches H1's 'pool shrinks first, then starvation' and not H3's 'DB slows first, then connections held'. H3 has no supporting log signature on the portfolio-service side of the ledger-db boundary.
